name: Pantoprazole + Itopride
meta: Pantoprazole Sodium: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI); Itopride Hydrochloride: Prokinetic (D2 antagonist + acetylcholinesterase inhibitor)
Pantoprazole Sodium: A02BC02; Itopride Hydrochloride: A03FA07
Schedule H – prescription only; Itopride Hydrochloride: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder (sodium sesquihydrate), freely soluble in water.
White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.

Pantoprazole Sodium: Has lower affinity for CYP enzymes than omeprazole, giving fewer drug interactions; preferred PPI with clopidogrel. First approval/introduction: Research began 1985 (Byk Gulden); Germany 1994; US FDA 2000 (Wyeth). Itopride Hydrochloride: Widely used in Asia for functional dyspepsia; its non-CYP metabolism minimises drug interactions and QT effects. First approval/introduction: Japan 1995 (Hokuriku Seiyaku / Abbott).
Acid suppression plus a prokinetic with no significant QT liability and minimal CNS effects (itopride is not CYP-metabolised).

Pantoprazole Sodium Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+-ATPase in gastric parietal cells, suppressing basal and stimulated acid secretion. Receptor / target profile: Prodrug activated in acidic canaliculi; covalently binds cysteine residues of H+/K+-ATPase.

Itopride Hydrochloride Dual action – dopamine D2 antagonism and acetylcholinesterase inhibition increase acetylcholine at the myenteric plexus, enhancing gastric motility and emptying; antiemetic. Minimal CNS penetration and no significant QT effect. Receptor / target profile: Dual D2 receptor antagonist and acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that increases acetylcholine and enhances gastric motility.
Summary: Bioavailability ~77%; Tmax 2–3 h (enteric-coated). ~98% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Half-life ~1 h (effect lasts >24 h).
Extensive hepatic N-oxidation by flavin-containing mono-oxygenase (FMO3, FMO1) – not CYP
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax ~0.5–0.75 h (SR prolonged). ~96% protein bound. Metabolised by flavin mono-oxygenase (FMO3), not CYP. Half-life ~6 h.
Functional dyspepsia (postprandial distress) with acid symptoms
One capsule once daily before breakfast
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Severe: max 20 mg/day (some labels 40 mg alternate days).
EE with GERD ≥5 years: 20–40 mg/day by weight.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk.
Hypersensitivity to pantoprazole or substituted benzimidazoles
GI haemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation
Long-term use: hypomagnesaemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, fractures
C. difficile diarrhoea, subacute cutaneous lupus
Drugs needing gastric acid for absorption (ketoconazole, atazanavir, iron salts)
May alter absorption of drugs due to faster gastric emptying
Pantoprazole Sodium: Magnesium on long-term use; B12 on long-term use.
Pantoprazole Sodium: Supportive care. Itopride Hydrochloride: Supportive care.
Holtmann et al., NEJM 2006 – itopride improved functional dyspepsia symptoms versus placebo; combination studies in GERD report additional symptom relief.
Swallow whole – do not crush or chew
Do not use long-term without review
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
